# kit-review

Read the diff and trace affected call paths. Review data handling, permissions, compatibility, error paths, async/resource cleanup, performance, dependencies and configuration in proportion to the change. Run applicable type/lint/build checks for evidence. Report each finding with severity, `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario and a suggested correction. Avoid speculative findings and do not turn a small edit into a full audit.

Review is read-only unless fixes are requested. Practices: [review practices](references/review-practices.md), [requesting a review](references/requesting-code-review.md), [receiving feedback](references/code-review-reception.md) and [verification before completion](references/verification-before-completion.md).

## Plan-driven work

Compare the diff and check evidence against the relevant phase's acceptance criteria and TODOs. Report incomplete work and proposed status corrections; the coordinator updates plan files. Request missing diff/log/test evidence from the coordinator when read-only tools cannot obtain it.

## --codebase

Review architecture and priority risks beyond a diff. Produce a prioritized improvement overview and phase files for actionable findings, following the `kit-plan` conventions; a read-only reviewer hands full contents to the coordinator to save. Do not apply repairs merely because review was requested, and do not create an empty plan when nothing is actionable.

## Receiving feedback

Verify each comment technically before acting: restate it, check it against the code, push back with evidence when it is wrong, and ask about unclear items before implementing any of them. No performative agreement.

Hand off the findings, checks run, changed paths (if fixes were requested) and remaining uncertainty.
